newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 22.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Eighteen-year-old minority Tamil refugee Chitra Rajendran, detained by police on suspicion of having links with separatist Tamil Tiger rebels, released by Colombo court.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga orders inquiry into alleged kidnapping and rape of a 10-year-old Tamil girl by security forces in the Jaffna peninsula.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas coordinate with the parliamentary group Sri Lanka Muslim Congress in matters regarding development of eastern province.
Defence Ministry denies allegations by some Tamil politicians that a 10-year-old Tamil girl was gang-raped by soldiers in Jaffna.
Security forces warn government VIPs not to attend functions in Jaffna as there was evidence of assassination attempts on them.
Police arrest six suspects who allegedly attempted to destabalise the country when they spread a false rumour that Colombo's water supply had been poisoned on the night of February 6.

Sri Lanka will be to the sub-continent what Hong Kong is to China now, with the emerging single common market in South Asia, Trade Minister Kingsley Wickremaratne tells visiting British trade delegation.
Attempt by LTTE to close schools in Jaffna for their Heroes Week unsuccessful, security forces say.

Sri Lanka to errect monument to commemerate those killed by left-wing JVP insurgents and government-sponsored anti-JVP death squads during the latter part of the 1980s, on December 10, which is World Human Rights Day.
Nine suspects arrested for spreading a false rumour that Colombo's water supply had been poisoned on the night of February 6.
